messages:
incident-bot: 🔴 INCIDENT DETECTED - dedpool-elara-01 GPU node gpu-7 thermal alarm -> automatic eviction started. Impact: Elara Systems dedicated pool. Pager: @Maya (oncall). node_id=gpu-node-7, pool=dedicated-elara, event=thermal-trip, severity=high
Maya (oncall): On it. Confirming scope — are active sessions being dropped or failing over?
Elara-Support: We saw a handful of 5xxs from their VPC endpoints ~30s ago. Customer reported degraded throughput on their batch jobs.
Maya (oncall): Ticketing note: starting live mitigation. Priority: isolate node, reroute tenant traffic, start drain.
Jason (eng-runtime): Realtime metrics show GPU temp spike to 105C then ECC errors. Kernel log snippet: ```[gpu-7] thermal_trip: sensor temp 105C -> throttle -> ECC err 0x4F``` Suspect fan/power.
Li (eng-platform): Kicking off drain now. Command: ```rctl drain-node --node gpu-node-7 --pool dedicated-elara --reason "thermal_trip" --force```. Expect 45-90s for active requests to finish, KV cache will be invalidated for that node.
Deploy-Bot: deployment activity: route-policy updated for pool dedicated-elara -> rule: route tenant elara-* away from gpu-node-7, started at 2401004340
Sam (solutions): Recommend enabling fallback to quantized-variant (q4_local) for Elara's long-running embeddings jobs while we replace node — less accuracy but keeps throughput. Sam -> Elara-Support: can y'all tolerate q4 for next 2 hours?
Elara-Support: Confirmed with customer ops: okay for inference pipelines but not for nightly evals. They accept: apply to production traffic only, keep evals pinned.
Maya (oncall): Hit list: 1) Confirm all active tasks offloaded 2) Mark node quarantined 3) Open hardware ticket with colo 4) Communicate ETA to customer.
Colo-Tech: Received hardware alert. Onsite tech en route to rack 14B. ETA 28 minutes. We'll try cold-restart after safe power cycle unless PSU replaced.
Jason (eng-runtime): Observed some evictions of long KV sessions. Running cache re-warm for critical models: ```rehydrate-cache --tenant elara --models core-* --parallel 4```. Should reduce cold-start latency.
Li (eng-platform): Node state now: quarantined=true, accepting_no_new_work=true, active_sessions=3 (draining). Drain progress: 88%.
Maya (oncall): Noted: two sessions are stuck on epoch checkpoint writes — touching Devs to accept graceful kill. @Jason can we force-resume them to next host?
Jason (eng-runtime): Force-migrate issued: ```migrate-session --from gpu-node-7 --to pool=dedicated-elara --session-ids 9876,9877```. One succeeded, one still retrying due to locked FS. I'll escalate to runtime team to unlock.
Sam (solutions): Preparing customer message: "We detected a GPU hardware fault isolated to one node in your dedicated pool and initiated automatic failover. Traffic has been routed away; fallback quantized models are active for production traffic. We'll update you with ETA for hardware replacement." Nina, please review before sending.
Nina (acct-mgr): LGTM. Add: "expected replacement in ~45-60 minutes; no config change required from your side." Sending now.
Elara-Support: Customer ops acknowledged and asked for status ping when node is physically power-cycled.
Colo-Tech: Onsite update: tech arrived, performed visual inspection. Fan assembly shows abnormal wear; fan RPM stuck. Attempted soft reset of BMC. BMC responded, but GPU temps unchanged. Proceeding to power cycle in 2 minutes.
Maya (oncall): Good. Plan after power cycle: if healthy, mark node back into pool with reduced load and monitor 10m; if not, we proceed to hot-swap/replace.
Deploy-Bot: power-cycle command executed at 2401004720 on gpu-node-7 by Colo-Tech. Reboot logs: ```POST: passed; driver init: ok; thermal-sensors: 72C -> cooling stable```
Jason (eng-runtime): After reboot, ECC errors ceased, temps settled to 72C. Running full diagnostics. Disk/driver errors show cleared. However GPU firmware reported a minor thermal stall on prior boot — recommend keep node quarantine for 15 minutes and run stress for 10m before rejoin.
Li (eng-platform): I'll keep node cordoned. Running stress test: ```stress-gpu --node gpu-node-7 --duration 600 --log /tmp/gpu7-stress.log```. Will post results.
Maya (oncall): Meanwhile, customer-facing routing remains on fallback. Anything else needed for tenant isolation?
Sam (solutions): One small item: disable cross-tenant cache sharing that could reintroduce stale KV entries from the quarantined node. Li, can you toggle cache isolation?
Li (eng-platform): Done: cache isolation flag set for dedicated-elara at 2401004825. All subsequent cache writes are tenant-scoped.
Colo-Tech: Stress test halfway: temps stable 78C, no ECC propagated. Fan RPM variable but within spec. Continuing to 10m mark.
Jason (eng-runtime): Stress finished clean. No ECC on stress run. Logs attached snippet: ```gpu7 stress complete: 0 errors, avg temp 76C, peak 79C```. I think it's safe to rejoin with reduced initial load.
Maya (oncall): Decision: reintroduce node into pool but with weight=0.25 for 30m, monitor metrics and customer error rate. If stable -> ramp to full. Li, enact.
Li (eng-platform): Routing update: rejoin gpu-node-7 to dedicated-elara with weight 0.25 at 2401004970. Telemetry hooks enabled for per-tenant latency and error rate.
Deploy-Bot: route-policy updated: gpu-node-7 weight=0.25, watch=true
Elara-Support: Customer ops reports throughput returning to normal within 2 minutes of rejoin. They want confirmation the fan will be replaced soon.
Colo-Tech: We'll schedule a replacement fan assembly during next maintenance window (within 24h). For now we recommend continued monitoring; if any relapse occurs we will escalate for immediate swap.
Maya (oncall): Closing loop: 1) impact contained, fallback models active for production only 2) node repaired/rebooted and rejoined at reduced weight 3) fan replacement scheduled 4) customer notified and acknowledged 5) post-incident follow-up owner: Jason (eng-runtime) to run root-cause and update runbook.
Jason (eng-runtime): Will own postmortem and update dedpool runbook for thermal-fault handling + add a playbook entry for immediate quantized fallback. Target postmortem draft by EOD.
Nina (acct-mgr): Customer thanked team for fast response. Tracking as sev-2 resolved for now.
Maya (oncall): Marking thread resolved in 30m if metrics remain green. Closing notes: great coordination — especially Colo-Tech for fast onsite. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: status=mitigated, update_ts=2401005455
